name: Question 9
problem:
Find ${e}^{At}$ for $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -5 & -2\end{aligned}].$ 

*Hint: The eigenvalues of $A$ are $\pm \text{i}.$*

| ${e}^{At}=\,\,$ |  | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)$ | {{field-1}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)$ |  |  |
worked_solution:
We have a square matrix of dimension $n=2.$ Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At} & ={\alpha }_{1}At+{\alpha }_{0}I \\  & ={\alpha }_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -5 & -2\end{aligned}]t+{\alpha }_{0}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & {\alpha }_{1}t \\ -5{\alpha }_{1}t & -2{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ are functions to be determined.

Consider the polynomial $r(\lambda )={\alpha }_{1}\lambda +{\alpha }_{0}.$ The eigenvalues or $At$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=\text{i}t,\,{\lambda }_{2}=-\text{i}t,
$$

which are complex conjugates. Thus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\text{i}t) & ={e}^{\text{i}t} \\ {\alpha }_{1}\cdot \text{i}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) \\ {\alpha }_{0}+{\alpha }_{1}\text{i}t & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we equate the real and imaginary parts, and solve for ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{0}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(t) \\ {\alpha }_{1}t=\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}=\frac{1}{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) \\ {\alpha }_{0}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ into the expressions for the required entries of ${e}^{At},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}t & =\frac{1}{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\cdot t \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) \\ -5{\alpha }_{1}t & =-5\cdot \frac{1}{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\cdot t \\  & =-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(t) \\ -5\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\end{aligned}].
$$
